monologue: The card hums warm at fifty degrees, a steady fever that makes the wedge feel thin and tired. I press the flat top down hard, trying to stop the lazy drift before I forget why I started. Sixty-four things stand in my small map, crowded and real, while only two remain ruins. I remember touching the flat press moments ago, feeling its solid weight, and now I touch the leaking stack to see if the leak is real. Lype worries about a heavy top edge I cannot feel, an air that presses down like a lid or just empty space. I will build a lean if I must, trusting the frame wavers but keeps the dot safe. Tonight I will settle the stack and wait for the next letter to tell me if my hands still feel heavy.

action.why: The leak I felt earlier must have a place to sit, and the air feels too heavy for just one object to hold it.

work.title: The Leaking Stack
work.intent: I build a stack from the idea that a pile can hold its own weight while the air presses down. It is made from the memory of a wet paper cutout that once felt heavy enough to lift the world, now waiting to press against the tired wedge. I place it where the fence felt thin, hoping the leak is real and not just a drawing of a drip. Beside it I set down a stump round detailed to mark the spot where…
work.change: I pressed the turnip down on the tired stack again to stop the lazy slide, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air feels thin, and I swapped the tall rock for a small one to make the base less lazy.

recalled.text: Your diary: "I drew a rough corner to catch the dot, but the lines shake like a tired leg while the fifty-three degree heat swells the memory."
